findings.title: Pump flag slots read a non-finite state (nan, inf, 1e309) as True: fault and defrost fabricated
findings.claim: inputs.parse_bool reads the states 'nan', 'NaN', 'inf', '-inf' and '1e309' as True (float(token) != 0.0), so a heat-pump fault or defrost entity reporting a non-finite number publishes fault=True and defrosting=True and freezes learning with freeze_reason 'pump_fault', where the numeric reader refuses the same state.
findings.mechanism: pump_signals.read -> InputReader.read_bool -> inputs.parse_bool: the numeric arm `return float(token) != 0.0` is reached for any token outside BOOL_TRUE/BOOL_FALSE, and float('nan') != 0.0 and float('inf') != 0.0 are both True. No finiteness test precedes it (const.finite_float, the integration's own number rule, refuses non-finite values), so an unreadable numeric state becomes a positive flag rather than `not_boolean`. The fabricated fault freezes every learner (`_learning_frozen`); the fabricated defrost feeds the defrost window/duty fold and blocks the COP fold.

evidence.unit: flag readings published True from a non-finite state (5 tokens x {fault, defrost})
evidence.machine: orchestrator Mac, Apple M1 (darwin arm64, 8 cores), shared box

findings.title: ECL110 MQTT state parser takes a JSON boolean as a displacement (true -> 1.0, false -> 0.0)
findings.claim: _parse_ecl110_state accepts the payloads 'true', 'false' and '{"displace": true}' as displacements 1.0, 0.0 and 1.0, and _async_handle_ecl110_state_message stores and publishes them as the measured ECL110 displacement, where const.finite_float refuses a bool as 'a guess, not a reading'.
findings.mechanism: json.loads('true') is the bool True; `isinstance(data, (int, float))` admits it (bool subclasses int) and `float(raw)` turns True into 1.0, so a state topic pointed at a switch/flag topic (ON/true) or a hostile publisher sets _ecl110_current_displace and the published ecl110_displace_command/ecl110_effective_displace to a value no ECL110 reported. The plausibility window (round-9 D1-s2-02) does not catch it: 0 and 1 are inside every window.

findings.title: An Open-Meteo sample stamped 0001-01-01 fails every solve: IrradianceSeries.mean_over overflows outside the fence
findings.claim: _parse_block keeps a sample stamped '0001-01-01T00:00', and IrradianceSeries.mean_over then raises OverflowError on `t - self.resolution` for every plan step, so every solve fails ('Optimization failed: date value out of range') for as long as the series is held, with last_update_success staying True.
findings.mechanism: OpenMeteoSolar.async_refresh fences only the fetch+parse (`_fenced`, #1519: 'never raises ... by construction'); the parsed series is stored, and the read side (`irradiance_for` -> `mean_over`, called per step by `_apply_open_meteo` inside the solve-input build) computes `sample_start = t - self.resolution` for every sample. datetime.min - 1 h raises OverflowError; async_run_optimization's broad handler books it as a solve failure (logged once by log_held, counted in _solve_failures), the last plan stays published and the update reports success. The series is replaced only by a later non-empty forecast, so a feed that keeps the stamp fails every cycle.

findings.title: _run_in_process's transport-failure arm waits unbounded on a killed worker while holding _PROCESS_LOCK
findings.claim: When the job write or reply read fails with a transport error (BrokenPipeError and kin), _run_in_process calls worker.kill() then worker.wait() with no timeout inside `with _PROCESS_LOCK`, so a child the kill does not end at once never returns and the lock stays held, while the sibling ProcessWorkerTimeout arm bounds the same wait with _SHUTDOWN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S for exactly that child.
findings.mechanism: coordinator.py `_run_in_process`: the `except Exception as err` arm (transport, never the job) does `worker.kill(); worker.wait()`; the `except ProcessWorkerTimeout` arm above it does `worker.kill(); worker.wait(timeout=_SHUTDOWN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S)` with the comment 'a child the kill does not end at once (one stuck in the kernel) must not turn this into the same unbounded wait'. One fact (how long to wait for a killed child) decided twice. Held, the lock wedges every later solve, replay and sensor-advisor job behind it (each parks an executor thread in `with _PROCESS_LOCK`), and the awaiting refresh never completes, so last_update_success never turns False. The same unbounded wait sits in _shutdown_process_pool's at_exit arm (coordinator.py ~1917).

evidence.unit: RESULT transport_lock_held_after (1 = _PROCESS_LOCK still held after the 8 s cap; transport_returned_within_cap=0)
evidence.machine: orchestrator Mac, Apple M1 (darwin arm64, 8 cores), shared box
evidence.contention_note: fan-out running; the cap is a deadline 160x the bounded arm's return, not a timing RESULT

findings.title: A persistently failing store save is logged only at DEBUG at all 17 persist handlers; state stops persisting
findings.claim: Every persist handler (17, persist_seams.py) catches any exception from building and saving its store payload and logs it only at DEBUG; with the save body forced to fail on every pass across setup, two refreshes, unload, restart and a refresh, each of the 10 handlers the lifecycle reaches added zero WARNING-or-higher records, so a payload-builder bug or a failing save silently stops the ledger, accuracy, thermal-learning, price-model, snapshot, away, legionella, notifier, off-restore and energy stores from persisting until a restart loses the unsaved state.
findings.mechanism: Pattern `try: await store.async_save(<payload built inline>) except Exception as err: _LOGGER.debug('Could not persist ...: %s', err)` in coordinator._async_save_{thermal_learning,price_model,ledger,accuracy,energy_totals,manual_plan,snapshots}, away.persist_override, boost.persist, dhw_learning.async_save_{profile,draws}, duty_switch._persist, legionella.async_save, notifier._async_save, off_restore._save, pump_arbiter._persist, debugger.DebugCollector.async_save. The payload is built inside the try, so a programming error in any learner's as_dict (an AttributeError, a non-serialisable value) is caught with the transport failures and logged below Home Assistant's default level on every cycle; nothing latches it (log_held exists for exactly this) and no repair issue is raised.

findings.title: _async_update_data's generic arm logs ERROR with a traceback on every cycle of a persisting failure
